status: DESIGN ONLY. No runtime doctrine has been changed.

new_concepts.name: Dispersed Air Defence
new_concepts.description: Swedish Bas 60 and Bas 90 planning dispersed aircraft and servicing units between wartime bases. Rapid repair sustains home defence, but duplicate ground services increase personnel costs and favour local operations.

new_concepts.name: Selective Air Denial
new_concepts.description: Finnish defensive choices and North Vietnamese controlled interceptions conserved a smaller fighter force. Selected engagements disrupt enemy operations, trading sustained air superiority and distant escort for local interception.

new_concepts.name: Offensive Counter Air
new_concepts.description: Israeli operations in 1967 demonstrated the value of rehearsed attacks against hostile air bases. Strike packages contest enemy air power at its bases, but high fuel demand and reduced home-defence emphasis persist.

new_concepts.name: Maritime Air Denial
new_concepts.description: Argentine attacks in 1982 showed how a regional air arm could threaten a stronger fleet. Maritime search and coordinated strikes prioritise the sea approaches, at the expense of land support and broad air-superiority operations.

new_concepts.name: Counterinsurgency Air Support
new_concepts.description: Portuguese operations in Africa used light aircraft and dispersed air support alongside troop operations. Persistent ground support favours a force facing limited hostile air power, but sacrifices fighter combat and strategic bombing.

new_concepts.name: Dispersed Servicing Teams
new_concepts.description: Swedish dispersed-base practice placed servicing teams and stores beyond a single main base. Mobile crews restore operations after disruption, while duplicated services need more personnel and complicate distant escort commitments.

new_concepts.name: Adversary Air Training
new_concepts.description: Aggressor training and Red Flag from 1975 exposed crews to unfamiliar aircraft and organised threats. Better combat preparation preserves experience, but flying the exercises consumes additional fuel and expensive instructor time.

new_concepts.name: Field Maintainable Designs
new_concepts.description: Swedish aircraft requirements favoured operation from dispersed sites with simple servicing. Maintainable tactical airframes reduce accidents and support demands, accepting a modest performance ceiling.

new_concepts.name: Rugged Attack Designs
new_concepts.description: Light attack and support aircraft served in Korea and the Portuguese African wars. Robust attack platforms emphasise ground fire and recoverability, sacrificing speed and air-to-air combat performance.

new_concepts.name: Tactical Airlift Procedures
new_concepts.description: The Berlin Airlift and later theatre transport operations relied on schedules, navigation and maintenance. Specialist transport crews extend practical reach and preserve loads, but cost more and take longer to qualify.

new_concepts.name: Maritime Search Coordination
new_concepts.description: Norwegian Orion operations from 1969 emphasised maritime surveillance and underwater search. Search crews exploit fitted sensors over wide approaches, accepting less strike emphasis and higher specialist personnel costs.

new_concepts.name: Low Level Penetration
new_concepts.description: Cold War strike crews trained for low-level penetration; RAF Tornado missions in 1991 also exposed its risks. Fast attack profiles improve strike survivability, but reduce range and bombing performance while increasing accident risk.

new_concepts.name: Stand Off Strike Packages
new_concepts.description: Late Cold War strike packages combined specialist support, designation and suitable weapons. Deliberate attacks gain reach and accuracy, but require costly crews and divert effort from immediate close air support.

new_concepts.name: Forward Air Control
new_concepts.description: Korean War airborne controllers and ground liaison teams coordinated aircraft near friendly troops. Better control strengthens close support, while specialist staffing and tactical priorities limit strategic bombing effort.

new_concepts.name: Sea Skimming Strike
new_concepts.description: Argentine pilots in 1982 attacked the fleet at very low altitude with bombs and missiles. Concentrated low approaches threaten ships, but short combat radius and the risk of low-level flight constrain the method.

new_concepts.name: Ambush Interception
new_concepts.description: Finnish defensive priorities and North Vietnamese ground-controlled attacks favoured selected opportunities. Fighters improve brief interception engagements, accepting weaker continuous air-superiority patrols and distant escort.

new_concepts.name: Section Mutual Support
new_concepts.description: Section tactics such as the Thach Weave in 1942 used teamwork to preserve weaker fighters. Mutual cover strengthens survivability and escort, trading individual attack freedom and ace generation for formation discipline.

new_concepts.name: Reconnaissance RPV Operations
new_concepts.description: Ryan reconnaissance drones in Vietnam and Israeli RPVs supported intelligence collection before modern armed UAV campaigns. Trained control and exploitation teams improve reconnaissance coordination, but need specialist staff and vulnerable unmanned platforms.

new_concepts.name: Decoy RPV Operations
new_concepts.description: Israeli RPVs in 1982 collected intelligence and served as decoys alongside manned strike packages. Coordinated support improves strike survivability and target preparation, at the cost of exposed decoys and additional control staff.

SWE: Swedish Armed Forces, wartime air-base history
Bas 60 and Bas 90, dispersion, alternate runways, ground units and protected command arrangements.
SWE_DESIGN: Manufacturer account: 1982 Gripen requirements included road operation and simple dispersed servicing. Later turnaround claims are not backdated to 1970.
FIN: General Heikki Nikunen, Finnish air-war account
Small fighter force prioritised bombers and avoided unnecessary fighter engagements; forward operating sites supported concentration.
VIE: National Defense University Press, Adapting to Disruption
Vietnamese ground-controlled, short-pass MiG tactics and adaptations during 1965-1968.
OCA: US Air Force history, Ideas, Concepts, Doctrine
1967 Israeli low-level attacks against airfields and the subsequent adaptation of opposing shelters and air defences.
ARG: Argentine maritime air attack, Exocet use, British airfield attacks and distant tanker/patrol support.
ARG_LOW: Military Review, A Sad and Bloody Business
Argentine wave-top attacks with conventional bombs as well as missiles; successes and limitations.
NOR: Norwegian Armed Forces Ombudsman, report to Parliament
333 Squadron P-3 introduction in 1969, maritime surveillance and demanding maintenance. Retrospective institutional source.
POR: Portuguese Air Force, Base Aerea No. 5 history
Combat deployments to Guinea and G.91 pilot preparation for African theatres in 1966-1973.
POR_CONTEXT: Portuguese Defence Ministry, African-war force and logistics study
Aircraft readiness difficulties, light aircraft under fire and introduction of additional aircraft in 1965-1966.
RED: Nellis Air Force Base, 414th Combat Training Squadron
Red Flag established in 1975 to supply realistic early combat experience before actual war.
FAC: National Museum of the USAF, Close Air Support in Korea
Airborne FAC and TACP coordination across USAF, Navy, Marines and ground forces in Korea.
LIFT: US Naval History and Heritage Command, Berlin Airlift
Airlift aircraft, scheduling, worldwide resource diversion and the 1948-1949 expansion.
LOW: Low-level airfield attacks, aircraft losses, transition to medium-level attacks and Buccaneer laser-designation support.
SECTION: US Naval History and Heritage Command, Thach biography
Mutual-support fighter tactics developed in the early 1940s and used at Midway in 1942.
RPV: US Army Combat Studies Institute, Eyes of the Army
Ryan reconnaissance RPVs, experimental armed work, Israeli development and the distinction from later operational UCAVs.
RPV_DECOY: Contemporary professional account of Israeli real-time reconnaissance and RPV decoys in 1982.
